requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.references.coverage.history`, and I found no adequacy gap.

**Coverage by evidence name, whatever the hash, including enclosing nodes and all three record kinds**
- `tests/references.rs#fn[items_named_by_recent_evidence_have_recent_coverage_whatever_their_hash]` uses an ordinary record, a citation review and a site review.
  - The citation review names `impl[Thing]`, which covers the method inside it.
  - The site review records a stale hash, and the item is still covered.
  - After the source is edited, coverage remains, so the recorded hash does not matter.
  - An unread item is the only one reported.
- `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_follows_the_outline_parent_chain_not_selector_text]` checks the parent-chain matching.
  - It matches the containing `impl[Thing]` and the root `""`.
  - It rejects an unrelated selector and a different file.
  - It rejects a `/` inside brackets that only looks like a prefix.

**Window of the current contents on disk plus the last N commits that changed the file**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` covers the default N of 3 and the `coverage.reauthored` example.
  - After two re-authorings the item is still covered.
  - After a third, `parse` is warned about.
  - The warning is not a validation error.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[uncommitted_records_count_as_they_are_on_disk]` covers `coverage.uncommitted`.
  - An uncommitted record that drops the item leaves it covered by the committed version.
  - An uncommitted new record covers the item before any commit.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[deleting_the_only_record_that_read_an_item_warns_at_once]` covers `coverage.deleted_requirement`: a deleted record has no window, so its item is warned about at once.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_merge_counts_only_when_it_differs_from_every_parent]` rules out counting every commit rather than only commits that changed the file. With N=2, a merge that takes the side branch's file unchanged is not counted, and the older version that read `parse` stays in the window.

**N from `[coverage] reauthorings`, which must be a positive integer, and 3 by default**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[the_window_follows_the_workspace_setting]` sets N to 1 and shows the older version drops out. It also shows that `reauthorings = 0` is rejected, and the error names `coverage.reauthorings`.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_invalid_coverage_table_is_a_validation_finding_but_authoring_proceeds]` rejects `0`, a string value and an unknown key.

**Read through a Git library, not by running `git`**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_history_uses_the_git_library_without_launching_git]` puts a tripwire `git` on `PATH` that fails every history-reading command. `status --coverage` still gives the correct answer, and the tripwire is never triggered.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` checks that validation does not read history.

**Unavailable history uses the available commits and is reported as incomplete**
- Shallow clones: `a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so`, `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete`, `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about`, `a_shallow_clone_holding_every_window_is_complete`, `a_linked_worktree_of_a_shallow_clone_knows_where_history_ends` and `an_uncommitted_record_does_not_make_a_full_shallow_history_incomplete`.
  - These show the window shrinks to the available commits and the incomplete flag is set.
  - They show `status --coverage` prints "Coverage history is incomplete".
  - They also show plain status does not print the incomplete notice, and the incomplete flag is not set when the clone holds the whole window.
  - This covers `coverage.shallow_clone`.
- Outside Git: `outside_git_only_the_files_on_disk_count_and_history_is_incomplete` covers the no-repository case.
- Unreadable history: `an_unreadable_historical_version_makes_history_incomplete` covers a missing blob, and `an_unlistable_evidence_directory_makes_history_incomplete` covers an unlistable evidence directory.

The historical-version tests all use ordinary records. Historical versions of citation reviews and site reviews are not tested separately. They are handled by the same window loader over the evidence files, and their naming and selector semantics are covered by the `tests/references.rs` test, so I treat this as a minor risk and not a gap.

text: :::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status --coverage` does not warn.
After a third such commit, no version in the window names it, and
`habeas status --coverage` warns about `parse`.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.deleted_requirement
Function `render` is read only by the evidence of `requirements.cli.render`.
The requirement and its evidence file are deleted.
Deleted files have no coverage window, so `habeas status --coverage` warns about
`render` at once, before any further commit.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.uncommitted
The evidence of `requirements.cli.check` read `parse`. The requirement is
re-authored but not yet committed, and the new record does not read `parse`.
The committed versions in the window still name it, so
`habeas status --coverage` does not warn. If the new record had read `parse`,
its contents on disk would cover it even before the commit.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{example} coverage.shallow_clone
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status --coverage`
says that coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents
do not cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
